inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E: 9M-2026 actual net sales 69,706 (Q1 21,861 + Q2 24,041 + Q3 23,804, Q3-2026 10-Q) plus Q4-2026E ~23,300 (Q4-2025 was 23,762 with Viterra consolidated). FY2025 (70,329) is a half-Viterra year (closed 2025-07-02), so compounding from it would require a fictitious +32% year-1; the combined-company run-rate is the honest FY0.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q3-2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted 194,049,036 (basic 192,289,837 + 1,759,199 dilutive awards); issued and outstanding 192,142,343 at 2026-09-30. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Buybacks are value-neutral here; $3.0B authorisation (March 2026) with $249M spent in 9M-2026 and none in Q3.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q3-2026 10-Q, 2026-09-30: short-term debt 6,471 + current LTD 1,331 + LTD 8,944 = 16,746; cash and equivalents 524. Operating lease obligations (480 current + 1,048 non-current) EXCLUDED: US GAAP operating lease cost sits inside EBITDA (treatment B). Readily marketable inventories (14,736 at fair value) are NOT netted -- see rmi_memo. Dec-2025 comparison: total debt 14,051, cash 1,135, net debt 12,916; the 3.3B rise since year-end funded a 3.4B inventory build (seasonal + price), which is why a Q4 stub-FCF bridge item is carried.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 reported FCF = OCF 844 - capex 1,723 = -879 (FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, lines 5763-5785); owner FCF = -879 - 73 SBC - 0 interest = -952. This is a working-capital-build year (inventories, margin deposits, Viterra consolidation) and is NOT the base the projections compound from. The component build gives a mid-cycle FY2027 owner FCF of ~1.5-1.6B (see assumptions.base and projections). Bunge's reported OCF swings between -5.5B (FY2022) and +3.3B (FY2023) on inventory price moves; only the component build is meaningful for a commodity processor.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was 202 (10-K line 4687) and 9M-2026 108, but Bunge is a net-debt company (16.2B); the income arises on operating balances (Argentine funding strategies, trade-structured finance, secured advances to farmers) and is netted against 586 of 9M-2026 interest expense. Not stripped -- there is no surplus cash pile being added to EV.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement 'Share-based compensation expense' 73 (FY2024 65, FY2023 69); 9M-2026 10-Q 70 (annualising ~95 = 0.10% of revenue). Bunge publishes no combined SBC+equity-award-tax line; net-share-settlement withholding is immaterial at this scale.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases 551 (kpis.buybacks); 9M-2026 249 (Q3-2026 10-Q line 2868), none in Q3-2026. The $3.0B March-2026 authorisation is not spent cash.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Friday); valuation written Sunday 2026-11-08, no after-hours print involved
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. CAPM for BG alone would be low (beta ~0.75, Rf ~4.2%, ERP 5% -> Ke ~8%), and with 46% market-value debt weighting (16.2B net debt vs 19.2B market cap) and A-/Baa1 debt at ~5.0% pre-tax / ~3.9% after-tax, a textbook WACC would print ~6%. House WACC set at 7.5%, which at the same weights implies a 10.6% cost of equity -- a ~2.5pp premium over CAPM that is the leverage/cyclicality charge the task asked for (post-Viterra gross debt 16.7B, variable-rate sensitivity 148M per 100bp, thin commodity margins). Charged ONCE: same WACC in all three scenarios; cyclicality itself is priced in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked again in the rate. Standard small-cap premium not applied (large cap).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): US GAAP operating lease cost (~548 principal + interest in FY2025, 10-K line 8795) is an operating expense already inside EBITDA/EBIT, so the margin paths carry it; operating lease obligations (1,528 at 2026-09-30) are excluded from net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already in the margin, not because leases are ignored.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows. Margins are calibrated to Bunge's 'Total EBIT', which by definition excludes EBIT attributable to noncontrolling interests (Q3-2026 10-Q Note 19; NCI EBIT 86 for 9M-2026). The NCI stock (1,506 + 78 redeemable at 2026-09-30) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.rmi_memo: The single largest framing question for BG. Rating agencies and management net readily marketable inventories (RMI, 14,736 at fair value at 2026-09-30) against debt to report 'adjusted net debt' of ~1.5B; the house model deducts full net debt of 16.2B because the RMI is the working capital that generates the EBITDA being discounted -- adding it back while keeping the EBITDA it earns would count it twice. The difference is ~76/share (14,736 / 194), which is the whole gap between this valuation and the market's framing. The market at 99.1 pays ~8.3x mid-cycle EBITDA on a full-net-debt EV (~34.7B); this model's base EV (~27B) is ~6.6x. Equity is a ~35% slice of EV, so each 10% move in EV is ~14/share.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (operating company, cyclical commodity processor -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. FY0 is an estimate (FY2026E) because of the mid-2025 Viterra close -- see base_revenue_note. Mid-cycle framing throughout: FY2026 adjusted Total EBIT ~3.1B (implied by $9.50 adj EPS midpoint, 24% ETR, 655 net interest guidance) is a strong-crush year with grain merchandising at a trough (9M segment EBIT 23) and 190 of 350 synergies realised; reported 9M Total EBIT 1,911. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin on 93B: ~4.5% adjusted, ~3.85% reported; base mid-cycle 4.0-4.1% sits between them, which calibrates to ~$8.4 mid-cycle EPS against the $8.50 standalone baseline management used pre-deal and a roughly EPS-neutral Viterra at mid-cycle. House and street bases nearly coincide (SBC 0.1% of revenue); band_position is therefore not meaningful for this ticker and should be read as 'collapsed'. US GAAP filer: no securitisation distortion in current OCF (the beneficial-interest line was 87 in FY2023 and nil since).

equity_bridge.item: Q4-2026 stub-period FCF (Oct-Dec 2026, between balance-sheet date and first projection year)
equity_bridge.note: Q4 is Bunge's seasonal working-capital release quarter. Q4 FCF (OCF less capex): FY2023 1,448-317 = 1,131; FY2024 1,053-489 = 564; FY2025 1,347-538 = 809; three-year average 835, rounded down to 800. Not in any projection year, so not a double count with year-1 wc_capture (which is on the FY2027-vs-FY2026 annual revenue change). Assets held for sale (European margarine business, net 487) deliberately NOT added: its EBIT remains in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run nominal revenue growth for a commodity processor (volume ~1-2% + price), applied after a 2.5% near-term step for Destrehan/Solae capacity; every historical CAGR is merger- or cycle-distorted
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 22.9% (6,205 FY2020 -> 17,369 FY2025) vs revenue 4.4% and EPS -23.6%: ~5.3B of the equity growth is Viterra share issuance (65.6M shares, July 2025) and ~1.5B is acquired NCI, not retained earnings. Ex-issuance equity CAGR is ~14% but still buyback- and cycle-distorted. Revenue CAGRs are commodity-price driven (FY2022 67.2B peak prices, FY2024 53.1B deflation, FY2025 70.3B half-Viterra). EPS 14.50 (FY2021) -> 4.95 (FY2025) reflects crush-margin normalisation plus 2025 integration costs and share issuance. None of these is a usable growth anchor; selected_growth_rate is a judgment.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2021 -3,354; FY2022 -6,169; FY2023 +2,117; FY2024 +459; FY2025 -952. CAGRs are undefined (negative endpoints) and would be meaningless anyway: the series is dominated by inventory price swings (FY2022 inventories build on record commodity prices, FY2023 release). The 'periods' here are 4 years for the 5yr revenue/EPS figures (FY2021 is the earliest revenue year under this CIK) and 5 years for equity (FY2020 book value is tagged).

base.growth_note: 2.5% for FY2027-29 (Destrehan line from Q4-2026, Solae assets, volume recovery in grain merchandising at flat prices), 2.0% thereafter = long-run volume plus modest price inflation.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA on net sales. FY2026E: ~4.5% adjusted / ~3.85% reported (strong crush, trough grain, 190 of 350 synergies, integration costs in Corporate). 4.0% in FY2027 as crush margins normalise from 2026 levels while synergies build, 4.1% from FY2028 = mid-cycle with full 350 synergies, normalised Corporate (-550), grain merchandising back to ~650 EBIT, soybean crush ~1.45B, softseed ~750, tropical oils ~150. Implies Total EBIT ~2.8B in FY2027 (vs FY2026 adjusted ~3.1B, reported ~2.5B) and mid-cycle EPS ~$8.4.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guided 1.5-1.7B (FY2025 10-K line 5119), 9M-2026 1,163. 1.5% (~1.43B) in FY2027 with Destrehan complete and Solae integration, stepping to 1.3% (~1.25x D&A) as the programme returns to maintenance plus modest growth.
base.cash_tax_note: Guided ETR 23-25% (Q3-2026). Cash taxes are running well below book (FY2025 186 vs 288 expense; 9M-2026 97 vs 390) on 100% bonus depreciation and acquisition timing; ramp 20% -> 23% over four years rather than perpetuate the shelter.
base.wc_note: Operating NWC (receivables + inventories + other current assets - payables - other current liabilities) was 13.7B at Dec-2025 (14.8% of run-rate revenue) and 17.0B at Sep-2026 (18.3%, seasonal peak). Capture -12% of the annual revenue change: growth consumes cash, deflation releases it. Sign is negative as the method requires for an inventory-heavy processor.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 7.5%/2.0% would be 18.5x FCF; capped at 15x, the top of the house 12-15x cyclical band given investment-grade scale and the ABCD oligopoly position. At the 15% hurdle Gordon (7.8x) binds instead.

bull.narrative: Margin 4.7% is roughly FY2026's adjusted level sustained, with synergies above 350 and grain merchandising recovering on top of it; growth 5% -> 2.5% is volume from Destrehan/Solae plus higher crush throughput and a firmer price deck. Capex stays higher (1.4%) because a bull Bunge keeps investing.

bear.narrative: Commodity deflation (-6%, -2%) releases working capital in years 1-2 (the wc_capture sign makes that automatic) but margins settle at 3.3-3.4%: a prolonged below-mid-cycle crush environment, not a permanent trough. Capex cut to ~1.1x D&A. Same WACC as base: risk is in the flows and the weight, not the rate.

scenario_narratives.base: Crush margins normalise from the strong 2026 level (biofuel-policy-supported soybean oil, record Q2-2026 soybean segment EBIT of 804) as US and South American crush capacity additions work through, while the Viterra synergy run-rate completes to 350 by 2028 and grain merchandising recovers from its 2026 trough (9M segment EBIT 23) toward a normal ~650. Net: Total EBIT ~2.8B in FY2027 against ~3.1B adjusted in FY2026, then grows with 2-2.5% nominal revenue. Capex steps down from the 1.5-1.7B Destrehan-era programme to ~1.25x D&A. Cash taxes ramp from the bonus-depreciation-shielded ~20% to 23%. Leverage stays elevated; the 15x terminal cap (vs 18.5x Gordon) and the full-net-debt bridge are what keep the equity value far below the market's RMI-adjusted framing.
scenario_narratives.bull: EPA RVO mandates and renewable-diesel feedstock demand hold crush margins near 2026 levels for several years, China's resumed US soybean buying normalises US origination, grain merchandising recovers to a Viterra-scale ~800 EBIT, and cost synergies run past 350 with commercial synergies on top. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 4.7% sustained; nominal growth 5% fading to 2.5% as Destrehan and Solae ramp. This is the case the current price requires -- bull IV is roughly the market price.
scenario_narratives.bear: RVO policy reversal or a crude-oil slide compresses vegetable-oil-driven crush margins at the same time as global crush overcapacity bites; grain merchandising stays depressed and Ukraine/Black Sea disruption recurs. Commodity deflation cuts revenue 6% then 2% (releasing working capital), but margins settle at 3.3-3.4% for the decade. With 16.2B of net debt against a ~18B EV the equity is a sliver: this is the Spruce Point leverage argument expressed in a DCF, and why the bear weight is 30% rather than the house 15%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the house 15%: equity is ~35% of enterprise value, so the leverage amplifies every operating miss, 2026 is a strong crush year whose repeat depends on biofuel and trade policy management itself calls 'in flux', and net interest (640-670 guided) consumes a quarter of mid-cycle EBIT. Bull cut to 20%: it needs sustained RVO-driven margins AND grain recovery AND synergy overdelivery together. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF for a leveraged commodity processor. The two decisions that drive the answer are (1) margin: 4.0-4.1% pre-SBC EBITDA sits between FY2026's reported 3.85% and adjusted 4.5%, i.e. a strong crush year is not extrapolated; and (2) the bridge: full net debt of 16.2B is deducted, with no credit for 14.7B of readily marketable inventories, because that inventory is the working capital earning the EBITDA. The market's RMI-adjusted framing is worth ~76/share and explains essentially all of the gap to the price. WACC 7.5% embeds a ~2.5pp cost-of-equity premium for post-Viterra leverage and commodity cyclicality, applied once across scenarios; the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin calibration: each 0.1pp of pre-SBC EBITDA margin is ~95M of EBITDA and roughly 7-8/share of equity value given the leverage; the mid-cycle call of 4.0-4.1% is a judgment between the reported and adjusted FY2026 run-rates

Readily marketable inventories: if one accepts the rating-agency view that RMI is cash-like, equity value rises by ~76/share; the model deliberately does not, and the finding is only as strong as that framing choice

Working-capital capture at -12% of revenue change: inventory value tracks commodity prices, so a sustained price rise consumes cash (and a fall releases it) in ways a revenue-growth proxy only approximates
Q4-2026 stub FCF bridge item (+800) rests on a three-year average of seasonal releases; a weak Q4 would remove ~4/share
Cash tax ramp 20% -> 23%: bonus depreciation could keep cash taxes low for longer (upside) or Pillar Two / Brazilian tax disputes (PIS/COFINS ~598M claimed) could push them higher
Base revenue is FY2026E, not an audited year; Q4-2026 net sales are estimated at ~23.3B
Terminal cap at 15x FCF (~6.6x EBITDA) is below the 8-10x EV/EBITDA the sector has historically traded at; uncapped Gordon at 7.5%/2% would add ~15/share to the base case
